short_description: Experimental mental-health trait retained for research inspection of depression-related score behavior within the strict no-imputation raw-array workflow; it is not consumer-ready.
summary_note: Experimental non-consumer mental-health trait used to inspect how a depression-related score behaves under the current strict raw-array workflow without imputation.
what_it_measures: A panel-relative polygenic signal associated with the bundled depression-related score, calibrated within the current local empirical reference panel for research inspection only.
interpretation_template: This is an experimental research-facing output, not a diagnosis of depression, not a screening result, and not a measure of current mental-health state. {interpretation}
caution_text: Experimental research output only. No imputation or ancestry-adjusted normalization is used, and the result should not be treated as a diagnosis, a screening result, or mental-health advice.
limitations: Percentiles and z-scores are relative to the local reference panel, not to a population-wide benchmark.
This trait is not consumer-ready and should stay in research review unless a separate product decision is made.

The source phenotype reflects a research depression-related measure rather than a clinical diagnosis, and real-world mental health depends strongly on life events, trauma, sleep, relationships, care access, and many non-modeled factors.
confidence_note: Confidence reflects overlap and reference robustness under the no-imputation raw-array workflow, not certainty about mental-health status.
reference_note: Percentiles and z-scores are calibrated against a local empirical reference artifact built from raw-array files in this project; they are panel-relative research values, not population-wide or clinical benchmarks.
